description: A late or duplicate response is delivered to the caller again
A finished request id is sent again
A timeout is reported as an error from the server
A server's cancel ends a listen as if the client cancelled it
Progress is accepted for a request that is not in flight
No hard timeout, so a request the server never answers stays in flight forever
A listen times out like any request
A server's cancel ends any request, not only a listen (REQ-05)
The wrong request ends: another request's grace runs out and ends a listen, which never had one
new:
/\ \E j \in Ids : Armed(j) /\ (~Timed \/ graceDue[j] <= now)
    /\ id \notin InitIds

description: No request ends: the grace runs out and nothing happens
A request sent after a refused line gets a grace from it
old:
SendGrace(id) ==
    /\ graceDue' = [graceDue EXCEPT ![id] = NoTime]
    /\ armedEpoch' = armedEpoch
    /\ graceTimers' = graceTimers
new:
SendGrace(id) ==
    LET late == GraceOn /\ refusals > 0 /\ id \notin InitIds \cup ListenIds
    IN /\ graceDue' = [graceDue EXCEPT ![id] = IF late THEN now + GraceTicks ELSE NoTime]
       /\ armedEpoch' = [armedEpoch EXCEPT ![id] = IF late THEN refusals ELSE NoEpoch]
       /\ graceTimers' = graceTimers + (IF late THEN 1 ELSE 0)

description: A request that finishes keeps its grace (a valid reply does not clear it)
Progress for another request clears this request's grace
new:
refusedAt[id] # NoTime]
    /\ graceDue' = [j \in Ids |-> NoTime]
    /\ graceTimers' = 0

description: Progress for the request's own token does not clear its grace
The error words carry what the server wrote
One timer per refused line, even when every request already has a grace
A second refused line extends the grace it finds
old: IF id \in Fresh THEN now + GraceTicks ELSE graceDue[id]
new: IF id \in Pending THEN now + GraceTicks ELSE graceDue[id]

description: initialize and listen get a grace too
